---
title: "Performance & Reliability"
---

IrisPipe separates **merge-gating regression tests** from long-running capacity benchmarks:

- **k6 Benchmark:** API/runtime latency, bounded data-volume behavior, failure semantics, and PostgreSQL-to-H2 coverage.
- **Backend K6 Checks:** 10 regression suites against a real Spring Boot backend.
- **RDBMS Compatibility Ring:** regular PR/main smoke coverage that starts each external database once, reuses those containers, and runs `H2 -> PostgreSQL -> Oracle -> MySQL -> SQL Server -> MariaDB -> H2`.
- **k6 Deep Volume Benchmark:** scheduled/manual retained capacity snapshots.
- **Full RDBMS Matrix:** six source-specific workflows covering H2, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, and Oracle. A full run is 6 sources x 6 destinations x JOB/CHUNK x 1M/10M/50M = **216 cases**.

## What the Benchmark Measures

The current benchmark profile is **`identity-relations-v2`**. It exercises a realistic three-table identity workload rather than a synthetic two-column table:

1. One IrisPipe SyncJob contains **three INSERT executions**: roles, users, then user-role assignments.
2. The executions become sequential Spring Batch steps inside the same job, so every benchmark case exercises IrisPipe multi-task orchestration.
3. Regular PR/main gates verify bounded H2-to-H2 JOB/CHUNK behavior and failure semantics.
4. The regular **RDBMS Compatibility Ring** reuses five already-started external DB containers and runs six heterogeneous hops at 10,000 total rows per hop. Every engine is exercised once as a source and once as a destination; JOB and CHUNK alternate around the ring.
5. Full matrix runs every source against every destination across H2 / PostgreSQL / MySQL / MariaDB / SQL Server / Oracle.
6. Capacity points are 1M / 10M / 50M **total migrated rows** for both JOB and CHUNK.
7. Destination correctness is verified **per table and in total**; a pipeline status of `COMPLETED` alone is not accepted as a pass.

All values are repeatable GitHub-hosted-runner regression benchmarks, **not production-capacity claims**.

---

## Benchmark Dataset Schema

The benchmark models a conventional users / roles / user-role relationship. Physical benchmark tables use `benchmark_src_*` and `benchmark_dst_*` prefixes so source and destination can coexist in one database instance for same-engine cases.

```text
users
  id            primary key
  username      varchar
  email         varchar
  display_name  varchar
  status        varchar   # ACTIVE / INVITED / SUSPENDED
  locale        varchar   # en-US / zh-TW / ja-JP
  created_at    timestamp/datetime
  updated_at    timestamp/datetime

roles
  id            primary key
  code          varchar
  name          varchar
  created_at    timestamp/datetime
  updated_at    timestamp/datetime

user_roles
  user_id       part of composite primary key
  role_id       part of composite primary key
  created_at    timestamp/datetime
  updated_at    timestamp/datetime
```

The benchmark intentionally omits database-enforced foreign keys. The logical relationship and composite key are real, but leaving FK checks out keeps the measured variable focused on IrisPipe orchestration, JDBC transfer, batching, and transaction boundaries instead of engine-specific referential-integrity enforcement cost.

### Row distribution

`ROW_COUNT` is the **actual total number of rows migrated across all three tasks**. Roles are fixed at 16 rows. The remaining rows are split 1:3 between users and user-role assignments, so each generated user has exactly three role assignments.

| Benchmark point | Users | Roles | User-role rows | Total migrated rows |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1M | 249,996 | 16 | 749,988 | 1,000,000 |
| 10M | 2,499,996 | 16 | 7,499,988 | 10,000,000 |
| 50M | 12,499,996 | 16 | 37,499,988 | 50,000,000 |

User payloads are deterministic, for example `{id: 123, username: "user_123", email: "user123@example.test", display_name: "User 123", ...}`. Role assignments are also deterministic and distribute three distinct roles per user across the 16-role set.

### Physical types and DB-side seed

| Database | User id | Role id | Datetime type | DB-side seed strategy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H2 | `BIGINT` | `INT` | `TIMESTAMP` | `SYSTEM_RANGE` |
| PostgreSQL | `BIGINT` | `INT` | `TIMESTAMP` | `generate_series` |
| MySQL | `BIGINT` | `INT` | `DATETIME(6)` | set-based Cartesian decimal digit sets |
| MariaDB | `BIGINT` | `INT` | `DATETIME(6)` | set-based Cartesian decimal digit sets |
| SQL Server | `BIGINT` | `INT` | `DATETIME2(6)` | digit CTE + `ROW_NUMBER()` |
| Oracle | `NUMBER(19)` | `NUMBER(10)` | `TIMESTAMP(6)` | bounded 10k `CONNECT BY` blocks |

Source data is generated **inside the database before timing starts**. k6 never sends millions of individual INSERT requests during setup.

## Multi-Task Pipeline Shape

A benchmark case is one SyncJob with three executions:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S["Source DB"] --> R["Execution 1: roles"] --> U["Execution 2: users"] --> UR["Execution 3: user_roles"] --> D["Destination DB"]
```

The steps are deliberately separate rather than one joined query. This means the benchmark validates that IrisPipe can coordinate multiple related migration tasks inside one job while preserving the configured JOB/CHUNK transaction semantics.

---

## Fetch vs Batch

IrisPipe exposes two independent tuning concepts even though the controlled benchmark currently sets them to the same value:

- **`fetchSize`**: source-side JDBC reader fetch window/hint. It affects read round trips, driver buffering, and memory behavior. It is **not** a transaction boundary.
- **`batchSize`**: destination-side writer batch/chunk size. In CHUNK mode it also defines commit boundaries; in JOB mode writes are still batched but all three executions share one destination transaction.

| CI profile | Source `fetchSize` | Destination `batchSize` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Regular PR/main benchmark | 1,000 | 1,000 |
| Deep/full benchmark | 5,000 | 5,000 |

Full/deep result tables display both values separately.

---

## JOB vs CHUNK: Transaction Boundary

With three executions, transaction grouping is slightly different from a single-table benchmark:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph JOB["JOB / 50M total rows"]
    J1["roles step"] --> J2["users step"] --> J3["user_roles step"] --> J4["1 destination transaction"]
  end
  subgraph CHUNK["CHUNK / 50M total rows"]
    C1["roles chunks"] --> C2["users chunks"] --> C3["user_roles chunks"] --> C4["commit each chunk"]
  end
```

For `batchSize=5,000`, CHUNK transaction groups are the sum of chunk counts for the three executions, not simply `ceil(totalRows / 5,000)`:

| Total rows | Roles chunks | Users chunks | User-role chunks | CHUNK transaction groups | JOB transaction groups |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1M | 1 | 50 | 150 | **201** | **1** |
| 10M | 1 | 500 | 1,500 | **2,001** | **1** |
| 50M | 1 | 2,500 | 7,500 | **10,001** | **1** |

The regular 10k failure case injects a duplicate composite key into the **final user-role row**. In JOB mode, the failure in execution 3 rolls back executions 1 and 2 as well, leaving only the pre-existing conflict row (**1 total row**). In CHUNK mode, the completed roles and users tasks remain committed, as do the first seven full 1,000-row user-role chunks; the failing final chunk rolls back, leaving **9,513 total rows** (16 roles + 2,496 users + 7,001 user-role rows including the pre-existing conflict).

## Benchmark Timing Boundary

Reported `duration_ms` / `rows_per_second` intentionally measure **IrisPipe migration execution**, not environment setup.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["DB/container startup"] --> B["Source seed"] --> C["Backend startup"] --> D["Pipeline config"] --> E["START TIMER"] --> F["POST /sync-pipeline\n3 Spring Batch steps + JDBC + commits"] --> G["STOP TIMER"] --> H["Per-table destination COUNT verification"] --> I["Publish report"]
```

**Included:** the synchronous `/api/v1/sync-pipeline` call from immediately before the request until the completed/failed response returns.

**Excluded:** database/container startup, source-data generation, backend startup/readiness, pipeline-config creation, post-run destination `COUNT(*)` checks, artifact aggregation, and Pages deployment.

`rows_per_second` uses the **total migrated rows across roles + users + user_roles** as the numerator.

---

## Throughput Chart Reading

The chart uses **X = total migrated row count on a log scale** and **Y = measured rows/second**. Each source database is a tab, each destination is a line, and JOB/CHUNK are separate tabs.

There are only three measured points: **1M / 10M / 50M**. For that reason the chart uses **straight line segments between measured points** and keeps the original point markers. It deliberately does not smooth, regress, or interpolate a curve between them.

## CI / Benchmark Triggering

Long-running 50M tests never block normal PR merges or ordinary `main` Pages deployment.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  PR["PR / main push"] --> G["Unit tests + regular k6 gates"]
  G --> C["RDBMS Compatibility Ring
5 shared external DB containers / 6 hops / 10k rows"]
  C --> P["Deploy Quarto using retained benchmark JSON"]

  T["tag: benchmark-full-*"] --> H2["Source H2 / 36 cases"]
  T --> PG["Source PostgreSQL / 36 cases"]
  T --> MY["Source MySQL / 36 cases"]
  T --> MA["Source MariaDB / 36 cases"]
  T --> MS["Source SQL Server / 36 cases"]
  T --> OR["Source Oracle / 36 cases"]

  M["Manual: Full RDBMS Benchmark - All Sources"] --> H2
  M --> PG
  M --> MY
  M --> MA
  M --> MS
  M --> OR

  H2 --> R["Serial merge into retained deep-performance-results.json"]
  PG --> R
  MY --> R
  MA --> R
  MS --> R
  OR --> R
  R --> D["repository_dispatch to GitHub Pages"]
```

Retained results are keyed by benchmark profile as well as DB pair, atomic level, mode, row count, fetch size, and batch size. This prevents historical single-table results from being mistaken for measurements of the current multi-table schema.

---

## Benchmark Methodology

1. `mvn package` runs backend unit tests before benchmark execution.
2. PR/main gates remain bounded; 10M+ capacity work stays in tag/manual/scheduled workflows.
3. The compatibility ring uses **10,000 total rows per hop**, `fetchSize=1,000`, and `batchSize=1,000`. PostgreSQL / Oracle / MySQL / SQL Server / MariaDB are each started only once with both source and destination tables, then reused for the entire cycle. This smoke layer is for SQL/JDBC/schema/reachability compatibility, not performance claims.
4. Full matrix jobs use `fetchSize=5,000`, `batchSize=5,000`, three INSERT executions, and 1M / 10M / 50M total-row points.
5. Source seed happens before the migration timer.
6. Destination counts are verified after the timer for roles, users, user_roles, and total rows.
7. Benchmark snapshots are merged into retained history by **benchmark profile**. Legacy single-table measurements remain available for traceability but are excluded from current-schema charts and coverage.
